clue.text: Cultured and calm, holding small cleaning item I flog

indicators.note: the word for calm holds the next pieces inside it, as a container grips its contents

parts.note: cool means calm, unflustered
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mop is an item used for cleaning floors
to tan someone's hide is to beat or flog them

explanation.surface: A refined, composed person who, oddly, sells mops for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flog' looks like 'sell' here, but it means beat, giving TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A worldly person familiar with many cultures is described as sophisticated and urbane, which is what cultured implies.

clue.text: Sad after rising workers' organisation fell

indicators.note: the word for sad comes after the reversed piece
in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the UK federation of unions
down means sad, low

explanation.surface: A trade union's members were left glum after a rising that fell flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress. 'rising' turns it into CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree is to chop it to the ground, the same as the phrasal verb used here.

clue.text: Really pretty housing with cheeky character

indicators.note: the two intensifiers house, contain, the joining word

parts.note: so means really, as in 'so good'
so also stands for pretty, fairly, as in 'not so bad'
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: A very attractive house belongs to a rascal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Really pretty' reads as praise, but each word is a separate SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A mildly insulting term for an annoying or impudent person, a rascal or cheeky character.

clue.text: One's clients expect delicacy when just out of bed

definitions.text: One's clients expect delicacy when just out of bed

parts.words: One's clients expect delicacy when just out of bed
parts.note: a restaurant's customers want shellfish freshly lifted from the seabed beds where they grow

explanation.walkthrough: 'just out of bed' suggests someone waking, but molluscs are farmed in beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant serving shellfish whose patrons expect them fresh from the beds is the venue described.

clue.text: They dry in spring time in this person's place

indicators.note: one letter goes in, taking the spot of another
the time letter takes the place of the setter's letter

parts.note: an oasis is a fertile spot fed by a spring in the desert
this person is the setter, I

explanation.surface: In springtime, something dries out at the speaker's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring time' reads as a season; split it: spring is OASIS, time is T, which replaces I.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilns used to dry hops are these buildings, typical of Kent, so they are things that dry.

clue.text: Trading, apart from Devon area, is dying

indicators.note: the word for trading is taken apart from the region, so those letters go

parts.note: switching is exchanging, trading one thing for another
Devon lies in the SW, the South West of England

explanation.surface: Commerce outside Devon is in terminal decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dying' looks like a gloomy report, but 'dying' means eager, as in dying to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impatient or eager to do something, as in 'longing to get started', is the same as dying to.

clue.text: Opposed to street neighbours once more

indicators.note: the street's abbreviation neighbours, sits next to, the other piece

parts.note: again means once more

explanation.surface: Residents of the street fall out with their neighbours yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition expresses opposition, as in voting contrary to a motion, so it means opposed to.

clue.text: What makes one ache, haggard — blooming marathon!

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it
drawn means haggard, tired-looking
flowers that are out are blooming

explanation.surface: A runner, aching and haggard, gasps about the marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' reads as a mild British swear word but means in flower, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon in the figurative sense is any event that goes on and on, tediously extended.

clue.text: Bans expenses after wife's accommodated for year

indicators.note: one letter is accommodated in place of another, so a swap is made in the word for expenses

parts.note: outlays are sums spent, expenses
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone stops paying costs once the wife has been housed for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link word here: the wife's letter is accommodated in place of the year's.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit something by law is to make it illegal, so the verb is a synonym of bans.

clue.text: Left-winger rejects first and second parties

indicators.note: the left-winger casts off part of the word, so letters are taken out

parts.note: a socialist is a political left-winger
first is written 1ST, and the 1 reads as I, giving IST
S is the abbreviation for second, the unit of time

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist snubs the first and second parties on the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' becomes IST because 1ST is read with the digit as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal gatherings or get-togethers, such as club evenings, are called socials, a plural noun meaning parties.

clue.text: Stretching one's legs out?

parts.note: taking a stroll while out cold, unconscious in sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like outdoors, but means asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking about while still asleep is a person stretching their legs while out for the count.

clue.text: From part of England, say, needing to go back or go west

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say must go back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
taken as written
to go west is slang for to die

explanation.surface: A puzzled instruction to someone from an English region: turn round or head west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go west' looks like a direction but is the idiom for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for a native of Tyneside, around Newcastle in north-east England, used here adjectivally.

clue.text: Nieces raging about carbon technology

indicators.note: the scrambled nieces go about, around, the element's symbol
the nieces are raging, wild, so their letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Nieces furious about the carbon footprint of modern technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raging' rearranges NIECES into SCIENE, and 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Technology is applied knowledge of the physical world, closely related to the systematic study it springs from.

clue.text: Performer on dobro offers classical piece

indicators.note: the words offer up, present, the run of letters concealed across them

explanation.surface: A musician playing a dobro, a resonator guitar, performs a classical work.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'performeR ON DObro'. A dobro is a steel-bodied resonator guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement with a recurring main theme, often the finale of a sonata or concerto, is a classical musical form.

clue.text: Raised in Belgium — coarse, backward place!

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
rough means coarse, unrefined

indicators.note: the word for place is written backward

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being raised in a crude, backward corner of Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' seems to insult the place, but it is the reversal signal on the word for place.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who was reared in a particular way was raised, the phrasal verb meaning nurtured.

clue.text: Exercises going into speech and action in theatre

indicators.note: the exercises go into, are placed inside, the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
PE, physical education, is school exercise

explanation.surface: Drama exercises built around speeches and stage action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage but means the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery carried out in an operating theatre is a procedure, the action a surgeon performs there.

clue.text: Staff go to join army

parts.note: a machine that works goes, functions
an army is a military force

explanation.surface: Employees are told to go and enlist in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: The employees of an organisation collectively are its personnel, the same idea as its staff.

clue.text: Words repeated in four-letter torrent undermining referee

indicators.note: in a down clue the torrent sits under the referee

parts.note: rain, a word of four letters, can fall in torrents

explanation.surface: A referee drenched by a torrent of four-letter words from the players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four-letter' suggests swearing, but just counts RAIN's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus in a song or poem, the lines sung again after each verse, is words that are repeated.

clue.text: Display uniform to wear after storming Spain

indicators.note: the scrambled letters wear, have on, the uniform's letter
storming suggests wild disorder, so the letters of after are rearranged

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Soldiers parade in uniform after storming Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storming' turns AFTER into FEATR, which wears U; E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A special item highlighted in a magazine or a shop is a feature, something put on display.

clue.text: Boxer with degree? Some might believe it

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a boxer with a university degree, and whether anyone would believe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of beliefs held as unquestionably true is something its followers believe, though not everyone does.

clue.text: Watercourses in deserts

definitions.meaning: long narrow channels dug for drainage

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the plural of a dug drainage channel and the verb for abandoning someone.

clue.text: Following golf, stayed and tidied up

indicators.note: the word for stayed follows the golf letter

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to room somewhere is to lodge or stay there

explanation.surface: After a round of golf, someone stopped over and smartened up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone neat and well turned-out has been groomed, made tidy in appearance.

clue.text: Curt with absent employee

parts.note: someone off work is absent
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Someone is short with a worker who failed to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: A brusque, casual manner that shows little interest is offhand, a synonym of curt.

clue.text: Where dancers go in galliard is contrariwise

indicators.note: the answer is in, contained within, the run of words

explanation.surface: Dancers head for a lively court dance that is done the opposite way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrariwise' suggests reading backwards, but the letters run forwards: galliarD IS COntrariwise. A galliard is an old court dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub for dancing to recorded pop music is the place dancers head for.

clue.text: Design of new arrow hitting king brought about end of conflict

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are brought about, around, the final letter
the anagram hits, runs up against, the king's letter
the letters of arrow are made new, rearranged

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

indicators.note: the end of the word conflict is its last letter

explanation.surface: A war story: a new kind of arrow striking a king ended the conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ARROW into ARWOR; 'hitting' puts K after it; 'brought about' wraps that round T, the end of 'conflict'.
explanation.definitionFit: Illustrations or graphic material in a publication are known as its design or artwork.

clue.text: The Bay Club pose oddly drinking from these?

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters of the words, the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Members of a genteel club strike a pose while sipping from their china.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading the odd letters of 'The Bay Club pose' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cups with handles are what one drinks tea from, so these vessels fit the cryptic description.

clue.text: Sadistic alien?

definitions.meaning: read playfully as not of our species, not a person

explanation.surface: Is the cruel creature from another world?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cruel and heartless, and literally not belonging to humankind, like a creature from space.

clue.text: Overlooked university censoring broadcast by journalist

indicators.note: letters broadcast are scattered, so the word censoring is rearranged

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A university's censorship of a journalist's broadcast went unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a noun about the media, but it is the anagram signal on 'censoring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passed over without being acknowledged or noticed has been overlooked, ignored.
